rationale: With no static profile available (empty source list, unknown function count) for this Prolangs-C++ benchmark, the table uses conservative, balanced defaults that favor low-cost, low-risk transformations over aggressive control-flow mangling. SUB and IGV get the highest SecurityGain weights because arithmetic/constant substitution is cheap, broadly applicable, and preserves correctness well, making them the security backbone. BCF and FLA receive moderate SecurityGain but the lowest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (i.e., their high cost sensitivity is respected) since bogus control flow and flattening carry the largest runtime and size penalties on unknown workloads; they will only fire on functions whose features strongly favor them. IBR and ICALL sit in the middle as moderate-cost diversifiers that add useful indirection-based resistance without dominating the overhead budget. SPLIT is weighted toward the cost/risk dimensions with the lowest benefit weights because it contributes little standalone resistance, acting mainly as a complement to FLA. All seven passes are enabled, letting the per-function feature matching decide actual application rather than hard-disabling anything given the absence of profile data.
